summary: Kootenai NF lookout near Eureka, MT: a 1939 pole first tower, a 45-ft steel live-in tower built 1983, staffed in summer, reached by a locked-gate service road.

facts.design: 45-foot all-steel live-in tower (1983); the first tower was a 35-foot pole L-4 (1939)

access.note: A locked gate blocks public motor vehicles on the service road, so visitors walk up. A 2022 visit found a sign listing open hours (9 AM to 6 PM, closed Wednesdays and Thursdays). Staffed each summer.

visit.trail_note: Park at the pullout before the locked gate on forestry road 7185 and walk the service road. Confirm open hours with the Kootenai National Forest; the 2022 visitor found the tower unmanned and climbing stopped at the stairs under the balcony.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

events.note: Site first used as a patrol point; the sources say only 'the 1920s'
Stanley Hanson working the lookout for the Forest Service, per a newspaper item quoted on Forest Lookouts
Smoker spot fire on Dodge Creek, under a hundredth of an acre; put out by a tanker truck
Gap-filler radar station completed at the lookout
Manned in September 1957; the newspaper called it the only manned lookout in the Rexford area
8x8 ft cab installed atop the radar installation, with no living quarters
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 9, 2021

corrections.why: Forest Lookouts, firelookout.com and the Forest Fire Lookout association's Montana list all say Lincoln County. Only the Register says Flathead, and the lookout is three miles southwest of Eureka, which is in Lincoln County.
L-4 describes the first tower, a 35-foot pole built in 1939. The present tower is the all-steel structure built in 1983.
The Register gives the present tower as 45 feet, about 13.7 m. The 2.4 m value matches no source read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three sources say Lincoln County and one says Flathead. The Eureka location supports Lincoln, so the record's Flathead value is proposed for correction.

notes_for_editor: Three conflicts for a human. (1) County: the Register says Flathead; the other sources say Lincoln. A correction is proposed, not applied. (2) Elevation: the Register gives 6,841 ft (2,085 m), firelookout.com gives 4,064 ft, and the 2022 visitor account gives 1,237 m. The record keeps the Register figure; this is unresolved. (3) Design and height: the brief's L-4 label and 2.4 m height describe the 1939 tower or match no source, so corrections are proposed. Access, the locked gate and the sign's hours come from one 2022 visitor account; recheck with the Kootenai National Forest before any visit guidance. Staffing as_of is 'undated' because the Register page has no date. The 1948 to 1957 entries come from a fan site quoting newspapers; the originals were not read. No rental was found for this lookout; the Recreation.gov Webb Mtn. rental is a different lookout.
